questions.stem: Select the three components of a Filter Condition: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A Filter Condition in ServiceNow consists of three components: Field (A) which specifies the column to evaluate, Operator (C) which defines the comparison type (equals, contains, greater than, etc.), and Value (D) which provides the comparison target. Together these form conditions like 'Priority equals 1'. Sum (B) is an aggregate function used in reports, not a filter condition component.

questions.stem: SLAs are used to ensure VUL are processed in a timely matter. Which field is used to determine the expected timeframe for remediating a VIT?
questions.explanation: The Remediation Target field on a Vulnerable Item determines the expected timeframe for remediation. SLAs in Vulnerability Response use remediation target rules that set a remediation date. A scheduled job 'Evaluate remediation targets' runs daily comparing the current date against this target date, updating the record status when approaching or past due.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create and change Service Level Agreements for Vulnerability Response groups?
questions.explanation: The sn_vul.admin role is the minimum required to create and change Service Level Agreements for Vulnerability Response groups. SLA creation is an administrative function within the VR application scope, requiring admin-level permissions. sla_manager (A) is a platform-wide SLA role but may not have VR scope access. admin (B) is the system admin which works but isn't the minimum. sn_vul.vulnerability_write (C) grants write access to vulnerability records but not SLA administration.

questions.stem: Changes made within a named Update Set in a different application scope:
questions.explanation: Changes made within a named Update Set in a different application scope will not be captured. Update Sets only capture changes within their own application scope. If you're working in the Vulnerability Response scope but your active Update Set belongs to the Global scope, changes to VR-scoped records won't be tracked. This is a fundamental ServiceNow scoping mechanism that protects application data integrity.

questions.stem: ServiceNow Vulnerability Response tables typically start with which prefix?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Vulnerability Response is a scoped application that uses the prefix sn_vul_ for all its tables. Examples include sn_vul_vulnerable_item (Vulnerable Items), sn_vul_entry (Vulnerability Entries/Third Party Entries), and sn_vul_third_party_entry. The 'sn_' prefix indicates it's a ServiceNow-developed scoped app, and 'vul' identifies the Vulnerability Response module.

questions.stem: In regard to the Security Operations Process, which of the following statements defines the “Identify” phase?

options.text: What processes and assets need protection?
What techniques can contain impacts of incidents?

questions.explanation: In the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the 'Identify' function focuses on understanding what processes and assets need protection. It develops organizational understanding of cybersecurity risk to systems, people, assets, and data. Detect (B) is about identifying incidents. Protect (C) covers safeguards. Recover (D) restores capabilities. Respond (E) contains incident impacts. The five functions are: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

questions.stem: Which module is used to adjust the frequency in which CVEs are updated?
questions.explanation: The NVD Auto-update module is used to adjust the frequency of CVE updates in Vulnerability Response. This scheduled job periodically pulls new and updated CVE data from the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) maintained by NIST. You can modify the schedule to control how often the update runs. There is no 'CVE Auto-update' (C) module — the correct terminology references NVD since that's the data source.

questions.stem: A list of software weaknesses is known as:

options.text: National Institute of Science and Technology (NIST)

questions.explanation: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) is a community-developed list of software and hardware weakness types maintained by MITRE. It serves as a common language for describing security weaknesses in architecture, design, or code. NVD (A) is a database of specific vulnerabilities, CVE (B) identifies specific vulnerability instances, and NIST (C) is a standards organization, not a weakness list.

questions.stem: Vulnerability Response can be best categorized as a ____________, focused on identifying and remediating vulnerabilities as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Response is best categorized as a proactive process. It focuses on identifying and remediating vulnerabilities before they can be exploited, rather than reacting after an incident occurs. By continuously scanning, assessing, and prioritizing vulnerabilities, organizations take preventive action to reduce their attack surface rather than waiting for security events.

questions.stem: If a customer expects to ingest 2 million vulnerabilities during its initial load, which instance size should you recommend?
questions.explanation: For an initial load of 2 million vulnerabilities, an XL (Extra Large) instance size is recommended. ServiceNow instance sizing for Vulnerability Response depends on the volume of vulnerability data being processed. L (A) handles smaller volumes up to approximately 1 million. XL (B) handles up to approximately 2 million. XXL (C) and Ultra (D) are for larger deployments exceeding 2 million items.

questions.stem: What Business Rule creates a Configuration Item from a Vulnerable Item record?

options.text: Create CI from Vulnerable Group Details
Create CI from Closed Item Details
Create CI from Vulnerable Item Details

questions.explanation: The 'Create CI from Vulnerable Item Details' business rule creates a Configuration Item from a Vulnerable Item record. When a vulnerability scan identifies a resource that doesn't exist as a CI in the CMDB, this business rule automatically creates the CI record using the details from the Vulnerable Item. Options A (from Vulnerable Group) and B (from Closed Item) don't match the standard VR business rule naming. Option C (Determine CI from Network) is not a standard VR rule.

questions.stem: The components installed with Vulnerability Response include:

options.text: Tables, Scheduled Jobs, Security Operations Common
UI Pages, Business Rules, Vulnerability Scanners

questions.explanation: Vulnerability Response installs Tables (sn_vul_vulnerable_item, sn_vul_vulnerability, etc.), Scheduled Jobs (NVD Auto-Update, vulnerability calculators), and depends on Security Operations Common as a foundational framework. Security Operations Common provides shared functionality like filter groups, integrations, and dashboards used across all SecOps apps. Options B, C, and D list components that exist within VR but don't capture the key dependency on Security Operations Common.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Scoped Applications?

options.text: Suppliers can only charge for applications when they are scoped
Scoped applications are scalable, Global applications are not
Scoping encapsulates and protects data and functionality
An application needs to be scoped in order to be deployed as a plugin

questions.explanation: Scoped applications encapsulate and protect data and functionality. Application scoping in ServiceNow isolates an application's resources (tables, scripts, business rules) within a defined namespace, preventing unintended access or modification by components outside the scope. This isn't about charging (A), scalability (B), or being a deployment requirement (D). Global applications also function properly; scoping adds an extra layer of protection.

questions.stem: What is the ID associated with the Vulnerability Response plugin?
questions.explanation: The Vulnerability Response plugin ID is com.snc.vulnerability. This follows the standard ServiceNow plugin naming convention where 'com.snc' is the ServiceNow namespace. com.snc.threat.intelligence (A) is for Threat Intelligence. com.snc.threat.feeds (C) is for threat feed data. com.snc.security_incident (D) is the Security Incident Response plugin. Each SecOps application has its own distinct plugin ID.

questions.stem: Where can you find information related to the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)?
questions.explanation: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) maintains the National Vulnerability Database (NVD), which is the primary source for CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) information. The NVD contains detailed analysis of each CVE including severity scores (CVSS), affected software, and remediation guidance. ServiceNow VR integrates directly with the NVD for vulnerability data. Tenable (A) and Qualys (D) are vulnerability scanners, not CVE databases. MITRE (B) maintains the CVE enumeration system but NVD provides the comprehensive data.

questions.stem: Which one of the following record types can be considered the intersection of Vulnerability source information and CMDB CI records?
questions.explanation: The Vulnerable Item (VI/VIT) record is the intersection of vulnerability source information and CMDB CI records. Each Vulnerable Item links a specific Vulnerability (from scanner data/Third Party Entries) to a specific Configuration Item in the CMDB, representing that a particular CI is affected by a particular vulnerability. This is the core operational record in VR.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides a list of software weaknesses?
questions.explanation: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) provides a categorized list of software weaknesses. It is maintained by MITRE and catalogs types of software security weaknesses (like buffer overflow, SQL injection). NVD (B) is a database of specific vulnerability instances (CVEs), not a list of weakness types. Third Party Entries (A) and Vulnerable Items (D) are ServiceNow VR record types.

questions.stem: Filter Groups provide a way to:

options.text: Decouple the use of the grouping from the definition of the grouping
Reuse criteria in a variety of places

questions.explanation: Filter Groups provide all of these capabilities: they decouple the use of the grouping from its definition (A), allow you to build criteria once (B), and reuse that criteria in a variety of places across the platform (C). Filter Groups are part of Security Operations Common and enable consistent, reusable filtering logic that can be applied to vulnerability groups, dashboards, reports, and other platform features without redefining the criteria each time.

questions.stem: Which module within the Vulnerability Response application could be used to get information from the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) at any moment?
questions.explanation: The On-Demand Update module within Vulnerability Response lets you fetch data from the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) at any moment. Unlike the NVD Auto-Update (B) which runs on a schedule, On-Demand Update triggers an immediate pull of NVD data when executed manually. This is useful when you need the latest CVE information without waiting for the next scheduled update cycle. Vulnerable Software (C) is a reference table, and NVD Patch (D) is not a standard VR module.

questions.stem: Which statement about patching is most correct?

options.text: Patch management and Vulnerability Response are interchangeable terms
Patching is one of many responses to a Vulnerability
As long as you are patching actively, Vulnerability Response isn’t necessary

questions.explanation: Patching is one of many responses to a vulnerability. Other valid responses include deferral/exception (accepting risk), compensating controls, configuration changes, network segmentation, or decommissioning the affected system. Mature organizations don't abandon patching (A), patch management is a subset of VR not interchangeable (B), and patching alone doesn't eliminate the need for VR (D).

questions.stem: The Vulnerability Admin role (sn_vul.admin) can modify Vulnerability Application Properties and can be delegated to the following role(s):
questions.explanation: The sn_vul.admin role (Vulnerability Response Admin) has full administrative access to VR application properties and configuration. This role can be delegated to multiple security-related roles including sn_sec.admin (Security Operations Admin), security.admin (Security Admin), and sn_vul_resp.admin. All of the above (D) is correct since all listed roles can receive delegation.

questions.stem: sn_vul.itsm_popup is the property that is set to True or False based on the customer desire for a popup when creating a Problem or Change record from a Vulnerability or VI record.
questions.explanation: The statement is True. The system property sn_vul.itsm_popup controls whether a confirmation popup appears when creating a Problem or Change record from a Vulnerability or Vulnerable Item record. When set to True, users see a popup confirmation dialog; when False, the record is created without the popup. This is a configurable application property in VR settings.

questions.stem: Items in the ServiceNow Store are built and supported by:

options.text: The company that created the Application

questions.explanation: Items in the ServiceNow Store are built and supported by the company that created the application. Third-party developers, technology partners, and ServiceNow itself publish apps to the Store, and each app is supported by its creator. ServiceNow does not provide technical support for third-party Store apps — the original developer/company maintains and supports their own applications.

questions.stem: Qualys asset tags can be loaded into a table related to the configuration item and used to support business processes or reporting. Set the Qualys Host parameter of asset_tags to a value of __________ to have asset tag information from Qualys be included in the XML payload.
questions.explanation: To include asset tag information from Qualys in the XML payload, set the Qualys Host parameter asset_tags to a value of 1. In the Qualys API integration, setting this parameter to 1 enables the inclusion of asset tag data in the host detection response, which ServiceNow then imports into a related table on the CI for use in business processes or reporting.

questions.stem: In ServiceNow, which plugin needs to be added to enable Vulnerability Integration with Qualys, Tenable, or Rapid7?
questions.explanation: The Vulnerability Response plugin must be installed to enable vulnerability integration with third-party scanners like Qualys, Tenable, or Rapid7. The base Vulnerability Response application provides the framework, tables, and integration points needed to import vulnerability data from these scanners. Additional scanner-specific plugins are then installed on top of the base VR plugin.

questions.stem: In order for Vulnerability admins to configure integrations, they must have the following Role(s):
questions.explanation: To configure integrations in Vulnerability Response, administrators need both the admin role and the integration-specific admin role such as sn_vul_qualys.admin. The base admin role provides system-level access for configuring REST connections and transform maps, while the integration admin role grants access to the integration-specific settings. sn_vul.admin alone (B) covers VR administration but may not grant access to integration-specific configurations. sn_vul.vulnerability_write (C) is insufficient for admin tasks.

questions.stem: In order to more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, what should you create?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Groups are used to manage large sets of Vulnerable Items by grouping them based on common characteristics such as the underlying vulnerability, affected CI type, or business service. This allows security teams to take bulk actions, track remediation progress, and assign work at the group level rather than managing individual VIs. Calculator Groups (B) and Vulnerable Item Conditions (D) are not standard VR features. Filter Groups (C) define reusable filter criteria but don't directly group VIs.

questions.stem: This functionality provides a simple way to build criteria once, which can be reused in other platform areas.
questions.explanation: Filter Groups provide a simple way to build filtering criteria once, which can then be reused in other platform areas such as vulnerability groups, dashboards, SLAs, and reports. They belong to the Security Operations Common framework and are shared across all SecOps applications. Conditions (A) are individual filter statements, not reusable groupings. Favorites (B) save personal list views. Filters (D) are applied to individual lists but aren't designed for cross-platform reuse like Filter Groups.

questions.stem: To facilitate the remediation of a Vulnerable Item what type of item is most commonly used?
questions.explanation: Creating a Change Request is the most common way to facilitate remediation of a Vulnerable Item. Since remediation typically involves applying patches, updating configurations, or modifying systems, these actions require formal change management approval to minimize disruption. Problems (A) identify root causes but don't directly remediate. Security Incidents (B) are for active threats, not scheduled remediation. KB articles (C) document solutions but don't execute the fix.

questions.stem: After closing the Vulnerable Item (VI), it is recommended to:

options.text: Update the values in the Vulnerability Score Indicator (VSI) based on the critically of the Vulnerability
The VI remains active and in place until the Scanner rescans and closes the VI
Mark the CI as exempt from the Vulnerability if the vulnerability was remediated
Compare the Vulnerability with subsequent scans

questions.explanation: After closing a Vulnerable Item, it is recommended to compare the vulnerability with subsequent scans to verify the remediation was effective and the vulnerability doesn't reappear. This confirms the fix persists over time and the asset remains secure. Updating VSI values (A) is not a standard post-closure step. Option B describes the normal closure process, not a post-closure recommendation. Marking the CI as exempt (C) is only appropriate if the vulnerability was accepted, not remediated.

questions.stem: Vulnerability Response is a scoped application; which prefix is attached to all items related to the application?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Response uses the scoped application prefix sn_vul for all its components. This prefix appears on tables (sn_vul_vulnerable_item), roles (sn_vul.admin), properties (sn_vul.itsm_popup), and script includes. The 'sn_' indicates a ServiceNow-developed application and 'vul' identifies the Vulnerability Response scope. Options cmn_vul (A), vul (B), and x_vul (D) are incorrect.

questions.stem: Which Vulnerability maturity level provides advanced owner assignment?
questions.explanation: The Improved Remediation maturity level provides advanced owner assignment capabilities. VR defines four maturity levels: Manual Operations (basic scanning), Improved Remediation (automated workflows, advanced owner assignment, SLAs), Automated Prioritization (risk-based scoring), and Enterprise Risk Trending (full analytics). Owner assignment automation is introduced at the Improved Remediation level.

questions.stem: Which application provides the opportunity to align security events with organizational controls, automatically appraising other business functions of potential impact?
questions.explanation: Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) provides the opportunity to align security events with organizational controls and automatically apprise other business functions of potential impact. GRC tracks organizational policies, controls, and risk indicators, allowing security vulnerabilities to be mapped to business controls and stakeholders to be notified when security events affect their areas.

questions.stem: Ignoring a Vulnerable Item:

options.text: Permanently removes the item from the list of Active Vulnerable Items
Move the item to the Slushbucket
Has no impact on the list of Active Vulnerable Items
Temporarily removes the item from the list of Active Vulnerable Items

questions.explanation: Ignoring a Vulnerable Item temporarily removes it from the list of Active Vulnerable Items. The VI record still exists in the system but is filtered out of active views. If the scanner detects the same vulnerability again in a subsequent scan, the VI can reappear. This differs from permanent removal (A) which would delete the record. It does have an impact on the active list (C is wrong). The Slushbucket (B) is a UI element for multi-select fields, not related to VI management.

questions.stem: What do Vulnerability Exceptions require?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Exceptions require an Approval by default. When a remediation owner requests an exception for a VI that can't be remediated immediately, they submit the request via the 'Request Approval' button, which changes the VI state to 'In Review' pending approval. The approval workflow is built into the standard VR exception management process. An Exception Workflow (B) exists but the key requirement is the approval. GRC integration (C) is optional. Filter Groups (D) are for filtering, not exceptions.

questions.stem: Best Practices dictate that when creating a Change task from a Vulnerable Item, which of the following fields should be used for assigning the Assigned To field on the Change task?

options.text: Best Practice does not dictate a specific field

questions.explanation: Best practices dictate using the Managed By field on the CMDB_CI record when assigning the Assigned To field on a Change task created from a Vulnerable Item. The Managed By field identifies the person responsible for the CI, making them the most appropriate individual to handle remediation changes. This ensures the change task routes to someone with authority and knowledge of the affected CI.

questions.stem: Approvals within the Vulnerability Application are created based on:

options.text: The sys_approval and the sn_vul_vulnerable_item tables

questions.explanation: Approvals within the Vulnerability application are created based on both the sys_approval and sn_vul_vulnerable_item tables. The sys_approval table manages the standard ServiceNow approval records (approver, status, comments), while the sn_vul_vulnerable_item table provides the vulnerability context for the approval request. Option D (sys_approval only) is incomplete as it doesn't reference the VR-specific table. Options B and C don't accurately describe the approval mechanism.

questions.stem:
Some customers may have a clearly-defined, well-documented vulnerability exception process and some may even provide a diagram illustrating that process.
What is the main advantage of having this documentation when translating it into a Flow or Workflow?

options.text: Build the Flow/Workflow directly into the platform

questions.explanation: The main advantage of having clearly-defined vulnerability exception documentation is to understand the customer's internal process. When translating an exception process into a Flow or Workflow, understanding the existing process ensures the automation accurately reflects the organization's established procedures, approval chains, and criteria. This understanding is the foundation before any platform building begins.

questions.stem: When an approval is rejected for a Vulnerable Item exception, what happens to the State field for that record?

options.text: It will be set back to its previous value

questions.explanation: When an approval is rejected for a Vulnerable Item exception, the State field is set back to its previous value. ServiceNow VR stores the previous state in the backup_state field before changing the VI to 'In Review' status during the exception request. If the approval is rejected, the state reverts to whatever it was before the exception was requested (e.g., Open, Under Investigation, or Awaiting Implementation). It does not default to a fixed state like Analysis (A), New (B), or In Review (C).

questions.stem: What option can be used to close out a Vulnerable Item Record or initiate the Exception Process?
questions.explanation: The Close/Defer option is used to close out a Vulnerable Item Record or initiate the Exception Process. When a VIT is deferred, the 'Request Exception' action triggers the exception workflow, setting the item to a Deferred state with a specified reopen date and reason. This is the mechanism for accepting risk or deferring remediation through the formal exception management process.

questions.stem: What must Vulnerability Exceptions be supplied by default?

options.text: Integrations with GRC to handle the exception
A manual approval authority for the exception

questions.explanation: Vulnerability Exceptions must be supplied with a reason for the exception by default. The exception request form has a required 'Reason' field with choices including Risk Accepted, Awaiting Maintenance Window, Fix Unavailable, Mitigating Control in Place, and Other. An 'Additional information' field is also required for providing detailed justification. GRC integration (B) is optional. Requirement Actions (C) are not part of the standard exception form. Approval authority (D) is configured separately in exception management settings.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a Vulnerability Group?

options.text: Groups VIs using a Filter against Vulnerable Item Fields
A Filter defining a sub-set of CIs to be treated as a group
The User Group assigned to resolving the Vulnerable Item
Must have a corresponding filter group

questions.explanation: A Vulnerability Group groups Vulnerable Items (VIs) using a Filter against Vulnerable Item fields. This allows security teams to organize and manage VIs based on shared characteristics like vulnerability type, severity, affected asset class, or business service. Option B describes a Filter Group, not a Vulnerability Group. Option C describes the assignment group on a VI record. Option D is incorrect because Vulnerability Groups don't require a corresponding Filter Group; they use their own filter criteria.

questions.stem: In order to more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, you would want to create:
questions.explanation: To more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, you would create Vulnerability Groups. These groups organize VIs by common criteria (such as vulnerability type, affected CI, or business service), enabling bulk actions, progress tracking, and workload assignment at the group level. Script Includes (B) are server-side reusable scripts, not for grouping VIs. Filter Groups (C) define reusable filter criteria but don't create VI groupings themselves. Vulnerability Sets (D) is not a standard VR feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the property that controls whether Vulnerability Groups are created by default based on Vulnerabilities in the system?
questions.explanation: The property sn_vul.autocreate_vul_centric_group controls whether Vulnerability Groups are automatically created based on Vulnerabilities in the system. When set to true, the system automatically generates Vulnerability Groups for each distinct vulnerability, grouping all associated Vulnerable Items together. Options B (autocreate_groups), C (autocreate_vul_grouping), and D (create_default_vul_groups) are not valid VR system property names.

questions.stem: What system property allows for the auto creation of Vulnerability Groups based on the Vulnerable Item’s Vulnerability?
questions.explanation: The system property sn_vul.autocreate_vul_centric_group allows for the auto creation of Vulnerability Groups based on the Vulnerable Item's Vulnerability. When enabled, each unique vulnerability automatically gets a corresponding Vulnerability Group containing all affected VIs. Options A (autocreate_vul_filter_group), B (autocreate_vul_approval_group), and C (autocreate_vul_group_item) are not valid property names in VR.

questions.stem: Where in the platform can you create Filter Groups?
questions.explanation: Filter Groups can be created at Security Operations > Administration > Filter Groups. Filter Groups are part of the Security Operations Common framework, shared across all Security Operations applications (VR, SIR, etc.). They are found under the Security Operations application navigation, not under the Vulnerability-specific menus. The Administration section provides the configuration interface for creating and managing Filter Groups. Options A, B, and D use incorrect navigation paths.

questions.stem: Which of the following can NOT be used for building Vulnerability Groups?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability records themselves cannot be used for building Vulnerability Groups. Vulnerability Groups are built using three methods: Filter Groups (predefined filter criteria), Condition Builder (defining conditions on the group form), and Advanced Scripts (script-based grouping logic). 'Vulnerability' is the data being grouped, not a tool or method for creating the groups.

questions.stem: Filter Groups can be used in Vulnerability Response to group what type of vulnerability records?
questions.explanation: Filter Groups in Vulnerability Response are used to group Third Party Entries (vulnerability records imported from scanners). By defining filter criteria, organizations can categorize and organize vulnerability data from third-party sources like Qualys, Tenable, and Rapid7 into logical groups for more efficient management, classification, and assignment of remediation work.

questions.stem: If fixing a Vulnerable Item outweighs the benefits, the correct course of action is:

options.text: Mark the CI inactive in the CMDB and notify the CI owner
Record the accepted risk and Close/Defer the Vulnerable Item
Deprioritize the Vulnerable Item Records (VIT) to push them further down the list so it can be ignored
Add the CI to the Vulnerability Scanner’s exclusions Related List

questions.explanation: When fixing a Vulnerable Item outweighs the benefits, the correct course of action is to record the accepted risk and Close/Defer the Vulnerable Item. This initiates the exception process, documenting the business justification for accepting the risk. Making CIs inactive (A), deprioritizing to ignore (C), or excluding from scanners (D) are all improper handling that loses visibility and accountability.

questions.stem: A common integration point with Vulnerability is:
questions.explanation: A common integration point with Vulnerability Response is Risk Indicators within GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance). VR integrates with GRC to feed vulnerability data into risk assessments, allowing organizations to quantify and track risk exposure. Workflow Mappings (A), Service Catalog (C), and Knowledge Base (D) are not primary VR integration points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common integration point between Vulnerability and GRC?
questions.explanation: Risk Indicators are a common integration point between Vulnerability Response and GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance). Vulnerability data feeds into GRC risk assessments through risk indicators that reflect the security posture of the organization. High vulnerability counts or critical unpatched systems generate risk indicators that GRC uses for risk scoring and compliance reporting. SIR (A), Change (B), and Problem (C) are ITSM integration points, not specifically VR-GRC integration.

questions.stem: What is the ServiceNow application used for process automation?
questions.explanation: Workflows (now Flow Designer) is the ServiceNow application used for process automation. Workflows/Flows automate multi-step processes including approvals, notifications, task creation, and conditional logic. Knowledge Base (A) stores articles, SLAs (C) track service level agreements, and Service Catalog (D) provides service request forms — none of these are process automation tools.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the Vulnerable Item State Approval Workflow?

options.text: It is read-only, you can only change the Assignment Group members for the approval
It exists in the Security Operations Common scope so it can be modified by any Security Operations Admin
It can only be modified by System Administrators

questions.explanation: The Vulnerable Item State Approval Workflow exists in the Security Operations Common scope, so it can be modified by any Security Operations Admin (sn_sec.admin). Since it resides in the shared Security Operations Common scope rather than the VR-specific scope, Security Operations administrators with appropriate scope access can customize the workflow to match their organization's approval requirements.

questions.stem: To ensure that Vulnerabilities are processed correctly, you can define a Service Level Agreement (SLA) for Vulnerability Response. To achieve this, you would:

options.text: Create a custom workflow to monitor the time between States
Log in as a system admin, and using the globally scoped baseline SLA Modules
Have the role of Vulnerability admin, but only in the Vulnerability Scope
Make sure you have at least the sn_vul.vulnerability_write role and using the baseline SLA Application Modules

questions.explanation: To define SLAs for Vulnerability Response, you need at least the sn_vul.vulnerability_write role and should use the baseline SLA Application Modules within the VR scope. This approach leverages the built-in SLA framework that ServiceNow provides for vulnerability remediation tracking. Creating custom workflows (A) is unnecessary since baseline modules exist. Using global scope (B) is incorrect because VR SLAs should be in the VR scope. Option C is incomplete as sn_vul.admin alone doesn't describe the method.

questions.stem: What role is required to view the Vulnerability Overview Dashboard?
questions.explanation: The sn_vul.vulnerability.read role is required to view the Vulnerability Overview Dashboard. This read-only role grants access to view vulnerability data, dashboards, and reports without the ability to modify records. sn_vul.manager (B) provides broader management capabilities beyond just viewing. sn_vul.ciso (C) is an executive-level role not required for basic dashboard access. sn_vul.vulnerability.write (D) grants write permissions which exceeds what's needed for viewing.

questions.stem: Managers should have access to which role-based data access and visualizations? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Managers should have access to Aggregations for priority and workload (A) to see the big picture of vulnerability distribution, Time period views (B) for tracking trends and progress over time, and Drill-down to granularity (D) for investigating specific areas when needed. Up-to-the-minute views (C) are more suited for operational teams who need real-time data for active remediation work, whereas managers focus on strategic oversight with aggregated and trend-based data.

questions.stem: To get useful reporting regarding the most vulnerable CI’s, which statement applies?

options.text: You must purchase a separate PA module
Your CI population must be huge
You must have good KPI’s defined
Your CMDB must be up to date and useful

questions.explanation: To get useful reporting on the most vulnerable CIs, your CMDB must be up to date and useful. Vulnerability Response relies on accurate CI data to correlate vulnerabilities with infrastructure. Without current CMDB data, VR reports cannot accurately identify which CIs are most at risk. A separate PA module (A) is not required, CI population size (B) is irrelevant, and KPIs (C) help but are secondary to data quality.

questions.stem: What type of data would the CIO/CISO want on the dashboard?

options.text: Single, clear indicators of organizational health

questions.explanation: The CIO/CISO wants single, clear indicators of organizational health on their dashboard. Executive leadership needs high-level, at-a-glance views showing overall security posture, risk trends, and compliance status rather than granular operational details. Aggregations (A) and drill-downs (B) are more suited for managers, and up-to-the-minute views (D) are for operational analysts.

questions.stem: The three levels of users you will likely encounter that will need access to data displayed in the Vulnerability Response dashboard are: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three levels of users needing VR dashboard access are Security Analysts (A) who investigate and triage vulnerabilities, CIO/CISO (C) who need executive-level security posture visibility, and Fulfillers (D) who perform the actual remediation work. Customers (B) are external parties who typically do not have access to internal vulnerability response dashboards.

questions.stem: What is the best way to develop a complete list of Vulnerability Reports?

options.text: Recommend that the client purchase the full Performance Analytics package
Work with the customer to identify the things that will be most useful to them
Use the standard out of the box reports only

questions.explanation: The best way to develop a complete list of Vulnerability Reports is to work with the customer to identify the things most useful to them. Each organization has unique reporting needs based on their security posture, compliance requirements, and stakeholder expectations. A collaborative approach ensures reports provide actionable value. OOB reports alone (D) rarely cover all needs, and buying PA (A) adds cost without understanding requirements first.

questions.stem: Filter Group configuration is found under which Application module?
questions.explanation: Filter Group configuration is found under the Security Operations > Groups application module. Filter Groups are a Security Operations Common feature shared across all SecOps applications, so they live under the Security Operations navigation menu. The Groups module provides access to both Filter Groups and other grouping mechanisms. Options B, C, and D place Filter Groups under the Vulnerability module, but they are actually a Security Operations-level feature.

Which is the property that is set to True or False based on the customer desire fora popup when creating a Problem or Change record from a Vulnerability or Vulnerable Item (VI) record?
questions.explanation: The property sn_vul.itsm_popup controls whether a popup appears when creating a Problem or Change record from a Vulnerability or Vulnerable Item record. When set to True, users see a popup confirmation dialog before the ITSM record is created. When False, the record is created directly without the popup. Note that options B and C have identical text; both show sn_vul.itsm_popup as the answer. Options A (popup_ui_page) and D (popup) are not the correct property names.
